title: ReorderableList
wrapsNative: List with ForEach.onMove(perform:) and EditMode (.environment(\.editMode, …) or EditButton), plus accessibilityActions(_:) and AccessibilityNotification.Announcement for each step
summary: A vertical list that people reorder by the row's reorder control. iOS provides it: a List whose ForEach has onMove(perform:), shown in edit mode. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a single column of rows whose order the person sets: pipeline stages, form fields, playlist items.
whenNotToUse: For tiles in two dimensions, use MonarchSortableGrid. For moving items between columns, use a Kanban board.
api: ForEach(_ data: Data, id: KeyPath<Data.Element, ID>, content: (Data.Element) -> Content).onMove(perform: (IndexSet, Int) -> Void)

states.name: editing
states.description: In edit mode each row shows the system reorder control at its trailing edge, which is the handle.

states.name: locked row
states.description: Use moveDisabled(true) on a row that cannot move.

appearance: System list appearance in every theme; rows inside a Monarch theme use the Monarch text styles and tint that the app applies.
platformNotes: The web ReorderableList draws its own handles, offers optional move buttons and announces every step in a live region. On iOS the system list already has a reorder control in edit mode, so Monarch ships no type; the recipe adds Move up and Move down accessibility actions that announce the new position. Android builds MonarchReorderableList because Compose has no built-in list reordering.
accessibility: The reorder control is the system's, with its own VoiceOver support in edit mode.
The recipe adds Move up and Move down accessibility actions to each row, so VoiceOver and Switch Control can move a row one place without a drag.
After each action the recipe posts an announcement with the new position: "Contacted moved to position 1 of 4".
Each row is one element with accessibilityElement(children: .combine).
edgeCases: EditButton and \.editMode exist only on iOS; the example guards them with #if os(iOS) so it also builds on the macOS host.
onMove gives a destination offset in the list before removal, which Array.move(fromOffsets:toOffset:) expects.
The Move up action on the first row and Move down on the last row do nothing.
